nicknames: The Sand Track of the Outback
Home of the Mount Isa Cup

main_sand.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise (left-handed). A specialized Outback Queensland sand oval with a short 300m home straight. The sand surface creates abrasive kickback, generating a massive natural bias toward early front-runners ('E') and pocket pressers ('P') who can command the rail away from sand spray. Deep closers ('C') suffer severe penalties.
main_sand.post_bias: CRITICAL INSIDE RAIL BIAS: In 900m, 1000m, 1100m, and 1200m sprint dashes, inside barriers (stalls 1–4) hold an immense advantage to grab the lead/rail and avoid sand kickback. Outer draws (7+) face heavy ground loss around tight bends.

handicapping_angles.outback_sand_surface_specialists: Mount Isa's sand surface is highly specialized. Heavily upgrade horses with proven track-and-distance form on Outback sand tracks (Cloncurry, Julia Creek, Richmond, Barcaldine). Be cautious with grass shippers making their sand debut without elite 1st-call gate speed (-3.0 pts).
handicapping_angles.extreme_front_running_kickback_bias: Over 78% of winners at Mount Isa race on or near the lead. Sand kickback is thick and abrasive; horses forced to race back in the field often yield. Aggressively upgrade lone early speed ('E') and tactical pressers ('P') drawn inside.
handicapping_angles.mount_isa_cup_carnival: During the Mount Isa Cup (1450m) feature meeting in May/June, staying toughness on sand is paramount. Factor in higher class offsets for Cup day feature races.
